definitions.explanation: One of the three main types of muscle tissue in the body. Skeletal muscles are attached to bones by tendons and, unlike smooth or cardiac muscle, are under voluntary control — they contract when we choose to move. They make up roughly 40% of body weight in healthy adults.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{骨格|こっかく}→骨格：06233_kokkaku⟧ (skeleton; body frame) and {筋|きん} (muscle). A formal, medical-sounding term used in anatomy, sports science, health writing, and nutrition articles. Emphasizes the muscles that move the skeleton, in contrast with the involuntary muscles of the internal organs and the heart.

USAGE:
Very common in fitness, rehabilitation, and aging-related health contexts, especially around topics such as sarcopenia (サルコペニア) and strength training for older adults. Body composition scales and medical reports often display {骨格筋|こっかくきん}{量|りょう} (skeletal muscle mass) as a separate figure from total muscle mass and body-fat percentage.

- {骨格筋|こっかくきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{鍛|きた}える→鍛える：12326_kitaeru⟧: to train the skeletal muscles

- {骨格筋|こっかくきん}⟦{率|りつ}→率：03802_ritsu⟧: skeletal muscle percentage (of body weight)

- {平滑筋|へいかつきん}: smooth muscle — the involuntary muscle of internal organs and blood vessels
